title: Findings on Improper Payments in Auditor-General's Report
what_it_is: Findings on Improper Payments in Auditor-General's Report

sections.label: Unmodified audit opinion given
sections.summary: The Auditor-General's Office gave the Government's Financial Statements an unmodified audit opinion this year, as in previous years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On the former, the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) has given the Government's Financial Statements this year an unmodified audit opinion, as has been the case in previous years.

sections.label: Procedural lapses, no fraud indicated
sections.summary: AGO highlighted procedural lapses, with no indication of fraud, misfeasance or dishonesty; cases involved overpayments and payments without prior approval, and agencies are recovering monies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: On the latter, AGO has highlighted in its report some areas in which there have been procedural lapses and where the Government agencies can do better.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: I should clarify at the outset that there is no indication in the AGO report of any payments due to fraud, misfeasance or dishonesty.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The cases highlighted by AGO this year largely concerned overpayments and payments made without prior approval, arising from human error, negligence or failure to follow established procedures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In each of these cases, agencies have been taking prompt actions to recover any monies which might have been erroneously paid out.

sections.label: When forensic inquiry is triggered
sections.summary: An audit precipitates forensic inquiry if there is reason, such as conflict of interests or systems allowing one person to approve, request and sign payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: An audit will highlight or precipitate forensic inquiry if there is reason to do a forensic inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if you go in and if you find there is conflict of interests, for example, payments to related third-parties or that your system as a whole enables the same person to approve a payment, submit a request for payment and sign a cheque for payment, that would require a forensic investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But if you go in and you find that there is, in MOH's case, a possibility of an overpayment which actually has not even occurred and you point it out and you can rectify it, and if the nature of that is because, as I have explained earlier, human error, negligence or non-compliance, that, in itself, does not trigger a forensic audit.

sections.label: Financial Statements fair and accurate
sections.summary: The Financial Statements of the Government are fair and accurate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this case, as I have explained earlier, the Financial Statements of the Government are fair and accurate.

sections.label: Rules adequate but not complied with
sections.summary: Rules and processes appear adequate but were not complied with in some cases, which does not necessitate a forensic investigation, so MOH's statement is correct.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this case, it would appear that the rules and processes are adequate, but, in some cases, they were not complied with that does not necessitate a forensic investigation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it is quite correct for MOH to say that the audit did not, in this instance, disclose evidence of fraud.
